text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch PTT backs away from taking stake in South African Telkom. (p1)
- Rabobank works on restructuring branch network. (p1)
- More Korean firms involved in Fokker takeover talks between Samsung and Dutch economic affairs ministry. (p3)
- Entertainment group Endemol takes over South African TV producer Toron International. (p3)
- Philips sheds 240 jobs in Krefeld, Germany to transfer them to Poland and Singapore. (p3)
- Bank insurer ING studies U.S. broker Merrill Lynch's bid for Australian stockbroker McIntosh Securities. (p3)
- Public TV advertising sales body STER says ad revenue dropped by 39 pct in the first ten months of 1996. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Cabinet needs more time to reflect on high-speed rail link. (p1)
- Liberalisation of electricity market forces utility companies to reorganise. (p2)
- Unions at DAF Trucks agree with company being taken over by U.S. Paccar. (p2)
- Chip producer ASM Int to launch on Amsterdam bourse with share issue. (p19)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Regional judges formulate policy on "golden handshake" for dismissed employees. (p1)
- Motor organisations forecast strong growth in number of cars on the roads to seven million by 2010. (p7)
- Shareholders' lobby VEB wants Endemol to clarify its involvement in sports-only commercial TV channel Sport7. (p27)
- Industrial group Stork sells Modular Pumps unit to Sweden's Johnson Pump. (p29)
TROUW
- Junior health minister Erica Terpstra says separate labeling of genetically-modified soya would not be useful. (p4)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Netherlands mulls damages claim against Israel for losses arising from delays to build Gaza sea port. (p7)
- KLM will not sell its stake in U.S. partner Northwest Airlines. (p11)
